clips.send: Gifts and trade goods. Porcelain and silk went out; spices came back. The fleet brought porcelain (fine “china” dishes), silk, tea and copper coins as gifts and for trade. Peaceful voyages: gifts and trade, not conquest.

clips.send: Chinese emperors are usually called by the name of their reign. Yongle (永乐 Yǒnglè, ruled 1402–1424) of the Ming sent Zheng He to sea and built the Forbidden City. Kangxi (康熙 Kāngxī, 1661–1722), Yongzheng (雍正 Yōngzhèng, 1722–1735) and Qianlong (乾隆 Qiánlóng, 1735–1796) of the Qing secured the borders. George Washington was US president during Qianlong’s last years.

clips.send: The Forbidden City. Built under the Yongle Emperor of the Ming: planned from 1406 and basically finished in 1420; the capital moved to Beijing in 1421. That is 72 years before Columbus sailed. The palace of 24 Ming and Qing emperors; today the Palace Museum. The largest and best-preserved ancient palace complex in the world (World Heritage, 1987): about 72 hectares (178 acres), roughly 135 football fields.

clips.send: Treasure ship. Flagship of the Ming fleet. From 1405 to 1433 Zheng He (郑和 Zhèng Hé) led a fleet to the “Western Oceans” (the seas west of the South China Sea) seven times. The History of Ming records that the largest treasure ships were 44 zhang long and 18 zhang wide (a zhang 丈 is an old unit of about 10 feet), which would make them longer than a football field. Historians still debate the exact size, but they were among the largest wooden ships of the age. Columbus’s flagship in 1492 was only about 60 ft (19 m) long. The fleet carried more than 20,000 people, as many as a small town, and set out from Liujiagang (in Taicang, Jiangsu Province, near today’s Shanghai). Zheng He: 1405–1433, seven voyages, 30+ countries, farthest to East Africa and the Red Sea.

clips.send: 1405年，一支两万多人的船队从中国出发——比哥伦布横渡大西洋早了87年，船也大得多。他们去了哪里？此后四百多年里，中国又发生了什么？明朝的郑和七下西洋，最远到达非洲东海岸和红海沿岸；紫禁城成为明清两代的皇宫；清朝前期收复台湾、抗击沙俄、平定准噶尔、管辖西藏，奠定了今天中国的辽阔版图。
